summary: L-4 cab on a 40-foot tower built 1936 in Snohomish County; abandoned 1957 and now gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1957. The register says it is now gone and the Washington lookouts index marks it removed. No removal date found.

staffing.status: staffed in 1942 (relief lookout described in an account Willhite relays)

visit.trail_note: Willhite has not visited the site yet. The only trail detail is a 1942 account of switchbacks, including one at Mile 13. No current route is described in the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Panoramic photos from August 12, 1935 show an unfinished timber tower at 26 feet. The register, firelookout.com and Willhite date the finished 40-foot tower with an L-4 cab to 1936. The timeline uses 1936 for the finished lookout.
Willhite's page is titled 'Glacier Creek Ridge Lookout'; the other sources use 'Glacier Ridge'. The record keeps 'Glacier Ridge'.

notes_for_editor: Built and abandonment dates agree across all four sources. Nothing read describes the site today, so the story says so and records no access level. The 1942 relief comes from an account Willhite relays from a book, not from a Forest Service record. Height 12.2 m is converted from the 40-foot tower in the register; it is not a surveyed figure. The firetower.org photos are credited to the National Archives, but no direct image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. The agency is taken from the national forest named in the register, since the administering line was not visible in the text read.
